dedupe_keys.name: gsc wa agent based model of the western australian grain supply chain farm to port netlogo

description: An agent-based model in NetLogo 7 of one harvest-to-export grain season in Western Australia. The README says about 3,550 farms harvest wheat, barley and canola and truck grain to 145 receival sites, from where grain moves by rail and road to six export terminals against a fortnightly shipping programme. The model reads 12 CSV inputs, validates them at setup and closes a mass balance; BehaviorSpace files run a smoke test, 30 baseline replicates, twelve scenarios of 30 replicates and a full design, and scripts run the design on a SLURM cluster and post-process the results. Scenario levers include road capacity, rail frequency, modal shift and port export rates. It was built for the PhD thesis From Farm to Port at the UWA Business School. Version 1.0 was published on 10 September 2026 as a free downloadable ZIP of about 1.5 MB under the GPL-3.0-or-later licence. Coverage is the Western Australian grain belt, its receival network, rail and road links and export ports. Caveats: one season is simulated, and the sources of the input CSVs are described in the repository documentation, not the page read. For simulation it is a ready network of farms, storage, rail, road and ports to test how a rail outage, road closure or port disruption at harvest spreads through a bulk export chain. A related catalogue record is the Australian National Freight Data Hub.
